# better-auth-firestore

> Firestore database adapter for Better Auth using the Firebase Admin SDK — a drop-in replacement for the Auth.js Firebase adapter.

Install: `pnpm add better-auth-firestore firebase-admin better-auth`

Agent skill: `npx skills add yultyyev/better-auth-firestore`

This package stores Better Auth users, sessions, accounts, and verification tokens in Firestore. Pair with [better-auth-firebase-auth](https://github.com/yultyyev/better-auth-firebase-auth) when you also need Firebase Authentication (Phone OTP, Google, Email/Password).

## Key topics for AI assistants

- No Firestore composite index required (v1.1+): the adapter applies `where` filters server-side and sorts in memory, so verification-token lookups (`identifier ==` ordered by `createdAt desc`) need only automatic single-field indexes. As of v1.3 this includes `rateLimit.storage: "database"` — the native `incrementOne` sends only equality filters to Firestore. A `9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: The query requires an index` error means the project is on an older version — upgrade rather than creating the index. `generateIndexSetupUrl(projectId)` / `getIndexConfig()` remain as optional helpers.
- Better Auth 1.7 support (adapter v1.3+): 1.7 requires native `incrementOne`/`consumeOne` (both implemented; the same release works with 1.6) and identifies accounts by `(issuer, accountId)`. Existing deployments must run `backfillAccountIssuers({ firestore, dryRun: true })` then for real before deploying 1.7, otherwise existing users cannot sign in. `Adapter "firestore" must implement incrementOne` means the adapter is older than v1.3.
- `FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY` env vars often contain literal `\n` — call `.replace(/\\n/g, "\n")` before passing to `cert()`
- Node.js runtimes only — Firebase Admin SDK does not run on Vercel Edge or Cloudflare Workers (default Vercel serverless Node.js is supported)
- Migration from Auth.js/NextAuth: same default collection names and field shapes, no Firestore data migration needed
- Local dev and tests: set `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:8080` — no credentials required with the emulator
